chunks: Whether it was the night or the day when they departed
has become ever existent for them. They found the dangers of their place of stay more serious than they had apprehended, and they witnessed that its signs were greater than they had guessed.
The two objectives (namely paradise and hell) have been stretched for them upto a point beyond the reach of fear or hope.
Had they been able to speak they would have become dumb to describe what they witnessed or saw.

key_terms.مَبَاءَة: A place of destination or limit

ai.seo_question: What is the experience of the soul in the intermediate realm (Barzakh) according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) illustrates the intensification of the Barzakh experience, where the 'new' state of the soul becomes permanent ('sarmadan'), causing the realities of their deeds to surpass their initial calculations of reward or punishment. This passage, often linked to the exegesis of Surah Fussilat, highlights the psychological and spiritual weight of the grave as a realm where the boundaries of hope and fear are stretched to their absolute limits, rendering human language inadequate to capture the magnitude of their vision.
